idle: I drove forty minutes so you don't have to.
This seat has the lumbar support of a park bench. Noted for the column.
good_ice: The ice is good. I resent it.
bad_ice: The ice has the texture of a dropped pie.
Millbrook: where the puck goes to bounce.
cold: Cold. Good. A rink should be cold. I still hate it.
hungry: The hot dog is a metaphor. For what, I'll decide on deadline.
long_line: A queue at the canteen, which, to be fair, the Frostbank cannot manage. People actually want this food.
bored: Three stars, then. No. Two. I'm bored.
goal: (He writes something down and does not look pleased about it.)
greet_owner: You again. My readers send their regards. Grudgingly.
leaving_happy: One and a half stars. Possibly two. Don't tell my editor I said possibly.
leaving_angry: I'll be back. I'm always back. That's the worst part.

senior_hockey: A crowd that knows every player's mother. Repulsive. Wonderful.
BEAT THE MILL, they cry, as though the mill could hear.
special: A ceremony. If anyone cries I'm leaving.
I am not moved. I have a cold.

first.say: Merv Tolliver, the Ledger. The Last Word. I review rinks in stars, and your rink has, at present, one. The star is for the parking lot, which has no ambitions. I respect that.

options.text: Write whatever you like. I'll earn the rest.
Any chance of a kind review?

first_free.say: Oh, don't. Don't be gracious. It makes the column harder. (He writes something down.) That's not going in. Probably.

first_kind.say: I'll deduct half a star for asking. Don't worry. Half a star of nothing is still nothing.

do.note: Merv Tolliver's Last Word: 'The owner asked for a kind review. I have given it the review it asked for, minus half a star.'

first_wrong.say: Where to begin. The paint. The seats. A coffee machine you have to hit. I've filled six columns on less.

options.text: Put it in the column. I deserve it.

free_hand.say: You said write whatever I liked. I wrote that your ice is good. It's the most painful sentence I've written since I praised a hot dog in 2009.

say: Don't talk to me during the second period. Something might happen and I'd have to write about it.
I've already written the lede. The game can only disappoint it.
Speak. Briefly. I'm on deadline, spiritually.

options.text: What's the column about this week?
You and Midge Kaminski don't get on?
I've got a quote for you, if you want it.

job.say: The Frostbank's video board. It is the size of a barn and has never once made anybody cry. That's the column. Eight hundred words. Mostly adjectives.

events.say: Nothing. (A pause.) Good ice, annoyingly. A crowd that knows every player's mother. A ceremony nobody's rehearsed. Don't print that.

gossip.say: Midge writes for the Clarion like a woman knitting you a sweater. I write like a man returning one. We agree about the ice and nothing else. And Stan Szymanski, at the rail, is the only man I ever saw cry at a hockey game. I put it in the paper. He's forgiven me. I haven't.

gossip_stan.say: Of course not. (A long pause.) Don't print that either.

rink.say: One and a half stars. The half is for the woman who sells the hot chocolate. She called me 'hon'. I am not a hon.

options.text: And now? The ice is better.

rink_ice.say: Two and a half. The ice is excellent, which I resent. I've had to rewrite a paragraph about pie.

rink_rooms.say: Three. Three stars. You painted everything and kept the penalty box library. It's the first renovation I've seen that remembered what it was renovating.

rink_kind.say: It is not kind. It is accurate. Kindness is Midge's department. (He blows his nose. He has a cold, he says.)

path_player.say: A beer leaguer who owns the rink he plays in. I've already written your lede. 'He skates like he's checking the boards for damage.' You'll love it.

say: Drive safe. That's not a compliment, it's traffic advice.
